extracted.intended_audience: professional observational astronomers and mathematical astronomers determining comet orbits (historical/technical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and observational/analytical rules to determine a comet's trajectory (parabolic/elliptic) from timed positional observations, including interpolation lemmas, geometric constructions, observational practices, accuracy expectations, and physical inferences about comet nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comet illumination: light reflected from the Sun
rubrics_metrics.description: Splendent igitur Cometæ luce Solis à se reflexa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary argument and observational implication: comet heads and tails are illuminated by reflected sunlight; maxima of head and tail brightness occur near solar vicinity and just after transit through solar rays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observed hemisphere bias due to solar illumination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex dictis etiam intelligitur cur Cometæ tantopere frequentant regionem Solis. ... quadruplo vel quintuplo plures detecti sunt in Hemisphærio Solem versus, quàm in Hemisphærio opposito.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect many more comet detections in the hemisphere toward the Sun because illumination makes them visible there; if comets lay far beyond Saturn they would more often appear opposite the Sun, which is not observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comets are not atmospheric meteors (free space bodies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc etiam manifestum est, quod cœli resistentia destituuntur. Nam Cometæ vias obliquas & nonnunquam cursui Planetarum contrarias secuti, moventur omnifariam liberrimè, & motus suos etiam contra cursum Planetarum diutissimè conservant. Fallor ni genus Planetarum sint, & motu perpetuo in orbem redeant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument from persistent systematic motion (including motion contrary to planetary motion) and long-term changes of heads shows comets are celestial bodies moving in orbits, not transient atmospheric phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comet structure: solid nucleus with atmosphere (coma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capita Cometarum Atmosphæris ingentibus cinguntur; & Atmosphæræ infernè densiores esse debent. Unde nubes sunt non ipsa Cometarum corpora, in quibus mutationes illæ visuntur. ... Et multo magis corpora Cometarum sub Atmosphæris & profundioribus & crassioribus abscondi debent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer the existence of a compact solid body (nucleus) surrounded by a comparatively dense atmosphere (coma); the visible 'clouds' are atmospheric features, not the solid body itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orbital form and area law for comets (conic sections, sun at focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometas in Sectionibus conicis umbilicos in centro Solis habentibus moveri, & radiis ad solem ductis areas temporibus proportionales describere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental assumption/proposition: comets move in conic sections with the Sun at the focus and sweep out areas proportional to time (Keplerian-style law used as basis for constructions). References to prior propositions for justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: If returning, comets follow ellipses with period scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc si Cometæ in orbem redeunt, orbes erunt Ellipses, & tempora periodica erunt ad tempora periodica Planetarum in ratione sesquialtera transversorum axium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a comet's orbit is closed, its period scales with the major axis as in planetary motion (example: axis 4× Saturn's ⇒ period 8× Saturn's ≈ 240 years). Use to estimate long periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parabola as practical approximation
rubrics_metrics.description: Orbes autem erunt Parabolis adeo finitimi, ut eorum vice Parabolæ absque erroribus sensibilibus adhiberi possunt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most practical computations the cometary orbit can be approximated by a parabola without sensible error — justifies parabolic trajectory assumption for many determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity scaling with distance (approximate formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: velocitas Cometæ omnis erit semper ad velocitatem Planetæ cujusvis ... in dimidiata ratione duplicatæ distantiæ Cometæ à centro Solis ad distantiam Planetæ à centro Solis quamproximè.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a rule for comet velocity relative to a planet's circular velocity near the Sun, scaling approximately with the inverse square-root (as implied by earlier propositions); used to estimate daily/hourly motions for graphical/arithmetic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a parabola through given points via finite differences (Lemma V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invenire lineam curvam generis Parabolici, quæ per data quotcunque puncta transibit. ... erit RS = a + b p + c q + d r + e s + f t &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: drop perpendiculars to a given line, form first/second/third differences (possibly scaled for unequal abscissas), choose a perpendicular RS and express its ordinate as RS = a + b p + c q + ... ; use the finite-difference progression to construct the parabolic curve through given points. Also implies that parabolas can be quadrated geometrically and used for area approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area (quadrature) approximation via parabolic fit (Corol. to Lemma V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hinc areæ curvarum omnium inveniri possunt quamproximè. Nam si curvæ cujusvis quadrandæ inveniantur puncta aliquot, & Parabola per eadem duci intelligatur: erit area Parabolæ hujus eadem quam proximè cum area curvæ illius quadrandæ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By fitting a parabola through sampled points of a curve, one can approximate the area (quadrature) of the curve; method relies on classical parabolic quadrature constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpolation of comet longitude/latitude at intermediate time (Lemma VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex observatis aliquot locis Cometæ invenire locum ejus ad tempus quodvis intermedium datum. ... Et si longitudinum observatarum parvæ sint differentiæ, puta graduum tantum 4 vel 5; suffecerint observationes tres vel quatuor ad inveniendam longitudinem & latitudinem novam. Sin majores sint differentiæ, puta graduum 10 vel 20, debebunt observationes quinque adhiberi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: from five observed longitudes construct a regular curve and find its ordinate RS giving the interpolated longitude at a given intermediate time. Practical guidance: if observed longitude differences between successive observations are small (~4–5'), 3–4 observations suffice; if differences are large (~10–20°), use five observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of chord/arc proportionality to time (Lemma VIII and corollaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si Cometa B moveatur in arcu CBA, & agatur ξB secans AC in E: dico quod punctum E abscindet de chorda AC segmentum AE tempori proportionale quamproximè.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction: for a parabola (trajectory) one may construct a chord segment AE approximately proportional to the time of arc described; supports mapping between measured chord lengths and elapsed times for constructing orbits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation of arc by chord at specified relative velocities (Lemma X, Corol.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometa igitur ea cum velocitate, quam habet in altitudine Sμ + ⅔ Iμ, eodem tempore describeret chordam AC quamproximè.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the specific altitude-based velocity at which chord length approximates the parabolic arc length — used to substitute chord lengths for arc lengths in time-based constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between free-fall descent and arc described (Lemma XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si Cometa motu omni privatus de altitudine SN ... demitteretur, ut caderet in Solem, ... idem tempore in orbe suo describat arcum AC, descensu suo describeret spatium longitudini Iμ æquale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates hypothetical radial descent under solar attraction to the arc described in the parabolic orbital motion; used in justifying constructions linking chord lengths, areas and times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining a parabolic trajectory from three observations (Prop. XLI, Prob. XX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometæ in Parabola moventis Trajectoriam ex datis tribus observationibus determinare. ... Seligantur tres observationes æqualibus temporum intervallis ... Si tales observationes non præsto sint, inveniendus est novus Cometæ locus per Lemma sextum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main practical rule: if you have three observations equally spaced in time (or nearly so, with specified ratio tolerances), use the provided geometric construction (form BE with AE:EC = V:W, draw circle through A,B,C, bisect chord AC, etc.) to find the parabolic orbit. If equal spacing is not available, use Lemma VI to interpolate a suitable point. The proposition gives a full step-by-step geometric construction to compute the orbit and determine nodes, inclination, perihelion, and latus rectum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-interval guidance for selecting three observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Seligantur tres observationes æqualibus temporum intervallis ab invicem quamproximè distantes. Sit autem temporis intervallum illud ubi Cometa tardius movetur paulo majus altero, ita videlicet ut temporum differentia sit ad summam temporum ut summa temporum ad dies plus minus sexcentos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative guidance for choosing observation intervals: for slowly moving comets choose slightly larger middle interval such that the difference of the intervals is to their sum as their sum is to roughly 600 days (complex heuristic). If not possible, use interpolation (Lemma VI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flamsteed's observational practice for improved accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: In his observationibus Flamstedius eâ usus est diligentiâ, ut postquam bis observasset distantiam Cometæ à Stella aliqua fixa, deinde etiam distantiam bis ab alia stella fixa, rediret ad stellam priorem & distantiam Cometæ ab eadem iterum observaret, idque bis, ac deinde ex distantiæ illius incremento vel decremento tempori proportionali colligeret distantiam tempore intermedio, quando distantia à stella altera observabatur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical observing protocol: measure distance to star A twice, then to star B twice, return to A and measure twice again; use the proportional change in distance over time to interpolate comet distance at intermediate times — reduces measurement error and provides consistency checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumentation and expected measurement precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Hæ observationes Telescopio septupedali, & Micrometro filisque in foco Telescopii locatis paractæ sunt: ... Micrometro parum affabre constructâ usus sum, sed Longitudinum tamen & Latitudinum errores (quatenus ab observationibus nostris oriantur) dimidium minuti unius primi vix superant, præterquam in observatione ultimâ Mart. 9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use telescopes with micrometer wires placed at the focus; with modest micrometer construction one can expect longitude and latitude errors not exceeding about 0.5' (half a minute of arc) under good conditions; note exceptional observations may be less accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphical/arithmetic processing: scale, chord tables and sine tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Hæc omnia per scalam partium æqualium & chordas angulorum ex Tabula Sinuum naturalium collectas determinavi graphicè; construendo Schema satis amplum, in quo videlicet semidiameter orbis magni (partium 10000) æqualis esset digitis 16⅓ pedis Anglicani.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process observations by graphical constructions on an ample scale, using chord tables and natural sine tables to convert angular measures to parts; choose a working scale (e.g., semidiameter = 10000 parts corresponding to a convenient physical size) to improve construction accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation by comparison of computed and observed positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tandem ut constaret an Cometa in Orbe sic invento verè moveretur, collegi per operationes partim Arithmeticas partim Graphicas, loca Cometæ in hoc orbe ad observationum quarundam tempora: ... Congruunt igitur observationes tam mense Novembri, quam mensibus tribus subsequentibus cum motu Cometæ circa Solem in Trajectoriâ hacce Parabolicâ, atque adeo hanc esse veram hujus Cometæ Trajectoriam confirmant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After obtaining an orbital solution, compute predicted comet positions for the observation times and compare with measured longitudes/latitudes; accept the orbit if computed and observed positions agree within expected combined observational and computational errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of observational and graphical errors (expectation & allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nam differentia inter loca observata & loca computata tam ex erroribus observationum quam ex erroribus operationum Graphicarum in Orbe definiendo admissis, facilè oriri potuere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When differences exist between observed and computed positions, attribute them to both measurement and graphical/arithmetic operation errors and allow for such discrepancies in judging the acceptability of the orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin and behavior of comet tails: heat-driven vapor emission
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducit igitur calefactio Cometæ ad magnitudinem caudæ. Et inde colligere videor quod cauda nihil aliud sit quam vapor longe tenuissimus, quem caput seu Nucleus Cometæ per calorem suum emittit. ... Porro si cauda oriretur ex refractione materiæ cœlestis, & pro figura cœlorum deflecteretur de Solis oppositione, deberet deflexio illa in iisdem cœli regionibus in eandem semper partem fieri.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observational tests: tails are largest and most luminous immediately after passage near the Sun (supporting heat-driven vapor emission). Tails lack color variegation expected from refractive phenomena; telescope amplification of star/planet light does not reveal tails, arguing against pure optical/refraction origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical inference: comets must be solid nuclei to survive perihelion heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Cometa igitur in perihelio suo calorem immensum ad Solem concepit, & calorem illum diutissimè conservare potest. ... Cometa hicce in transitu suo per viciniam Solis statim dissipari debuisset. Est enim calor Solis ut radiorum densitas, hoc est reciprocè ut quadratum distantiæ locorum à Sole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thermal reasoning: given extreme solar heating at perihelion, comets must be solid/durable bodies (not mere vapors) to avoid immediate dissipation; use scaling of solar heat with inverse square of distance and thermal conduction arguments to infer nucleus solidity and heat retention times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple independent observers and cross-checking for reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Præterea cum Cl. Flamstedius Cometam ... primò cum amicis communicavit, & postea easdem ad examen revocatas calculo diligentiore correxit. Nos loca correcta hic descripsimus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: share and compare observations among independent observers, re-examine and correct positions with more careful computation when discrepancies arise; prefer observations from more careful/accurate observers when conflicts exist.
